_comment: Accepted high/critical npm advisories for the OpenCode plugin roster.
Read by tools/supply-chain/audit-plugins.sh. Measured 2026-08-20.
Re-verified and extended 2026-11-07 (EOP-257/258/259): the four entries
introduced by @tarquinen/opencode-smart-title were deleted with that
plugin's removal, the two seroval entries were refreshed, and seven new
entries were added after tracing each one (seroval x3, toml x3, zod x1).
SCOPE. This file governs high and critical advisories only, because those are
the only severities that fail the audit. Low and moderate findings are reported
and not gated, so they must NEVER be listed here -- an entry for one would be
unfireable and would rot into a claim nobody checks.
WHAT AN ENTRY MEANS. Exactly one thing: a human read the advisory, traced the
vulnerable code path through this repository's actual runtime, and established
that it is not reached. It does not mean the advisory is wrong, that the
dependency is trustworthy, or that the finding may be ignored next time. Write
the trace into `reachability` in enough detail that a reviewer can falsify it
without repeating the investigation -- name the file, the symbol and the guard.
AN ENTRY IS A LIABILITY, NOT A DISMISSAL. The script fails when an allowlisted
advisory is NO LONGER reported, and fails when its severity or module stops
matching. That is deliberate: the usual failure mode of a suppression list is
that it outlives the thing it suppressed and silently starts hiding something
else. Here, an advisory that gets fixed upstream turns the job red until the
entry is deleted. Deleting a stale entry is routine; adding one is not.
WHAT IT CANNOT DO. Unreachable today is not unreachable tomorrow. Every entry
here rests on a runtime fact (which JavaScript engine loads the plugin, which
branch a lazy `require` sits behind) that no test in this repository pins. A
dependency bump that starts calling the vulnerable API would not fail this
audit -- the advisory would still be reported, still be allowlisted, still
match. Re-verify the trace when a pin moves, and prefer moving off the
dependency to carrying an entry indefinitely.

GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c.title: Seroval: `fromJSON()` Promise thenable assimilation invokes plugin-produced callables (bypass of GHSA-mv8w-475r-vwqw)
GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c.reachability: Not reached. seroval is imported only by solid-js/web/dist/server.js (lines 3-4), the SSR server-rendering entry, which pulls Serializer from seroval and plugins from seroval-plugins/web. Nothing in the installed DCP/@opentui tree imports solid-js/web at all: DCP is a terminal-UI plugin built on @opentui/solid, which renders to the terminal and never server-renders HTML, and solid-js's `node` export condition resolves the package root '.' to ./dist/server.js, the core server build, which imports no seroval. DCP's own dist/, lib/ and tui code reference seroval, hydrate, fromJSON and deserialize nowhere. This advisory is a defect in seroval's fromJSON() deserialisation path, reachable only when the SSR serializer revives untrusted input -- a path this tree never loads.
GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c.no_fix_available: There is no in-range upgrade. seroval is pinned by solid-js: solid-js@1.9.12 declares `seroval ~1.5.4`, and even the newest 1.9.15 declares the same range, which excludes every patched release (1.6.1 fixes this critical, 1.6.3 the paired high). DCP 3.2.0 (newest stable) declares `solid-js ^1.9.12`, a range that admits fixed solid-js 1.9.16+ (seroval ~1.6.8), but @opentui/solid@0.4.5 -- the version DCP 3.2.0's `^0.4.5` range resolves -- peer-declares solid-js exactly 1.9.12, and a scratch install on 2026-11-07 confirmed resolution keeps solid-js 1.9.12 and seroval 1.5.6. @opentui/solid 0.8.x loosens the peer to ^1.9.12, but DCP's range caps at 0.4.x. No repo-side override is possible: OpenCode generates its own per-plugin manifest under ~/.cache/opencode/packages/@tarquinen/opencode-dcp@3.1.15/ and runs npm install itself, so nothing committed here reaches that install. The named exit is the move to Sleev, DCP's upstream successor, tracked separately.

GHSA-jp82-f5mq-hwhp.title: Seroval: Memory exhaustion via unchecked TypedArray length in JSON deserialization
GHSA-jp82-f5mq-hwhp.reachability: Same trace as GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c: a defect in seroval's JSON deserialisation path, imported only by solid-js/web's SSR server-rendering entry, which this terminal-UI plugin tree never loads.
GHSA-jp82-f5mq-hwhp.no_fix_available: See GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c -- seroval is pinned to ~1.5.4 by solid-js, and DCP 3.2.0's solid-js ^1.9.12 range is held at 1.9.12 by @opentui/solid@0.4.5's exact peer (verified by scratch install 2026-11-07).

GHSA-7rv5-mrxv-xcr9.title: Seroval: Deserialization invokes attacker-chosen callables: AsyncIteratorFactoryInstance calls source.on(listener) without type check
GHSA-7rv5-mrxv-xcr9.reachability: Same trace as GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c: this is a deserialisation-time callable-invocation defect in seroval, which is imported only by solid-js/web/dist/server.js, the SSR server-rendering entry. The DCP/@opentui terminal tree never imports solid-js/web, solid-js's `node` export condition resolves '.' to ./dist/server.js (no seroval import), and DCP's dist/, lib/ and tui code invoke no seroval deserialisation entry point (fromJSON, fromCrossJSON, deserialize). The vulnerable path -- reviving untrusted input through the SSR serializer -- is never loaded.
GHSA-7rv5-mrxv-xcr9.no_fix_available: See GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c -- seroval is pinned to ~1.5.4 by solid-js 1.9.12, held in place by @opentui/solid@0.4.5's exact solid-js peer; no in-range release of any package in the chain moves it.

GHSA-97r2-qh9m-474h.title: Seroval: fromJSON deserializer trusts node-supplied array length and sequence doneAt (unauthenticated event-loop DoS)
GHSA-97r2-qh9m-474h.reachability: Same trace as GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c: a defect in seroval's fromJSON() deserializer, imported only by solid-js/web/dist/server.js (SSR). The DCP/@opentui terminal tree never imports solid-js/web and never calls fromJSON/fromCrossJSON/deserialize, so node-supplied lengths from untrusted input are never read.
GHSA-97r2-qh9m-474h.no_fix_available: See GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c -- seroval is pinned to ~1.5.4 by solid-js 1.9.12, held in place by @opentui/solid@0.4.5's exact solid-js peer; no in-range release of any package in the chain moves it.

GHSA-wp97-x4hv-qvhp.title: Seroval `fromJSON`/`fromCrossJSON` denial of service via unvalidated array node length
GHSA-wp97-x4hv-qvhp.reachability: Same trace as GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c: a defect in seroval's fromJSON/fromCrossJSON deserialisation (~1.4.1-1.6.7), imported only by solid-js/web/dist/server.js (SSR). The DCP/@opentui terminal tree never imports solid-js/web and never calls either deserialiser, so unvalidated array node lengths are never processed.
GHSA-wp97-x4hv-qvhp.no_fix_available: See GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c -- seroval is pinned to ~1.5.4 by solid-js 1.9.12, held in place by @opentui/solid@0.4.5's exact solid-js peer; no in-range release of any package in the chain moves it.

GHSA-4qx8-w7c3-pj3p.title: toml-node: Quadratic-complexity DoS via many array-of-tables headers in toml.parse()
GHSA-4qx8-w7c3-pj3p.reachability: Not reached. toml is required by exactly one file in the tree: effect/dist/unstable/cli/Primitive.js:353 (`const {default: Toml} = require("toml")`, collected into the fileParsers map and read only by Primitive.fileParse). No file outside node_modules/effect/ references unstable/cli, and @opencode-ai/plugin's dist imports no effect subpath (its imports are @opencode-ai/plugin, @opencode-ai/sdk and the effect package root), so dist/unstable/cli/index.js -- the entry that would load Primitive.js -- is never resolved. The vulnerable function Toml.parse() is never invoked. All three toml advisories below share this trace.
GHSA-4qx8-w7c3-pj3p.no_fix_available: There is no fixed release. @opencode-ai/plugin@1.19.5 is the newest release and declares effect 4.0.0-beta.83; effect@4.1.2 (newest 4.x prerelease line) still declares `toml ^4.1.1`, and the reported range <=5.0.0 covers every 4.x release, so no version in any declared range escapes it.

GHSA-9j65-hcg3-gc64.title: toml-node: Quadratic-complexity DoS via long dotted keys or table paths in toml.parse()
GHSA-9j65-hcg3-gc64.reachability: Same trace as GHSA-4qx8-w7c3-pj3p: toml is required only by effect/dist/unstable/cli/Primitive.js:353 (fileParsers map / Primitive.fileParse), which nothing outside node_modules/effect/ reaches -- @opencode-ai/plugin imports no effect subpath -- so Toml.parse() is never called.
GHSA-9j65-hcg3-gc64.no_fix_available: See GHSA-4qx8-w7c3-pj3p -- @opencode-ai/plugin@1.19.5 is the newest release, effect@4.1.2 still declares toml ^4.1.1, and the range <=5.0.0 covers all 4.x.

GHSA-9qmh-m7c6-f92p.title: toml-node: Uncontrolled resource consumption (CPU DoS) via unbounded-length integer literals in toml.parse()
GHSA-9qmh-m7c6-f92p.reachability: Same trace as GHSA-4qx8-w7c3-pj3p: toml is required only by effect/dist/unstable/cli/Primitive.js:353 (fileParsers map / Primitive.fileParse), which nothing outside node_modules/effect/ reaches -- @opencode-ai/plugin imports no effect subpath -- so Toml.parse() is never called.
GHSA-9qmh-m7c6-f92p.no_fix_available: See GHSA-4qx8-w7c3-pj3p -- @opencode-ai/plugin@1.19.5 is the newest release, effect@4.1.2 still declares toml ^4.1.1, and the range <=5.0.0 covers all 4.x.

GHSA-h895-cgqg-jf52.title: toml-node: Prototype pollution: parsing a TOML document can write to Object.prototype
GHSA-h895-cgqg-jf52.reachability: Same trace as GHSA-4qx8-w7c3-pj3p, re-verified against the installed tree on 2026-11-11: the only import of toml is effect/dist/unstable/cli/Primitive.js:14, and Toml.parse(content) is called only at line 353 by the fileParsers map used by Primitive.fileParse. No pinned plugin or @opencode-ai/plugin dist file references effect/unstable/cli, Primitive.fileParse or Toml.parse, so the parser module and its prototype-polluting parse path are never loaded.
GHSA-h895-cgqg-jf52.no_fix_available: There is no in-range upgrade. @opencode-ai/plugin@1.19.5 is still the newest release and pins effect@4.0.0-beta.83 exactly; that Effect release declares `toml ^4.1.1`, which resolves to 4.3.0 and cannot select the patched 5.0.1. Reaching the fix requires an upstream @opencode-ai/plugin release that moves its exact Effect pin or otherwise removes or updates TOML. Changing only this repository's generated audit manifest would not change the real plugin install.

GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5.title: Zod can exhaust memory while validating oversized constrained collections
GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5.reachability: Not reached. The defect requires an actual validation call (parse / safeParse / parseAsync) over a large constrained collection. After smart-title's removal the only importers of zod in the tree are @opencode-ai/plugin/dist/tool.js, which assigns tool.schema = z (schema construction only, the schema is handed back to the host and never validated here), and opencode-goal-plugin's src/goal-plugin.js:17, a dead import with zero `z.` uses anywhere in that file. No schema-validation call exists in the remaining tree: the only parses present are JSON.parse and goal-plugin's own flagSpec.parse, neither of which is a zod entry point.
GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5.no_fix_available: There is no in-range upgrade. @opencode-ai/plugin@1.19.5 is the newest release and pins zod@4.1.8 exactly, so the root node cannot move. opencode-goal-plugin's newest release (0.11.4) does declare a fixed zod (4.6.7), but upgrading it would still leave zod@4.1.8 in the tree via @opencode-ai/plugin, and this advisory would keep being reported. The remaining exit is an upstream @opencode-ai/plugin release that lifts its exact zod pin.
